findings.reason: The protected source is already the canonical median-coordinate solution. Its row-major and column-major comprehensions obtain both coordinate lists in sorted order without sorting, and its two deviation sums directly realize the separable Manhattan optimum. It is concise, conventional, and candidate-free.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 296 and its Python binary-grid-to-integer contract. The Reference preserves the Manhattan-distance objective, both source examples in order and the sole explanation, all five constraints including at least two homes, and an accessible text equivalent of the source grid image.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064355362. It and the app-local source have identical sorted row and column collection orders, upper-median selection, and absolute-deviation sums; only the required wrapper and type syntax differ.

The legal 64/256/1024-cell square tiers span 16x, distribute 9/34/133 homes, and exercise full grid scans and nontrivial deviation sums. The current source passes at -0.02 relative exponent and 1.01x largest ratio; a correct implementation that evaluates every grid cell against every home passes all outputs but fails only scaling at +1.04 and 77.56x.

The Approach now defines grid dimensions m and n and home count k before the manifest bounds, proves coordinate separability and the one-dimensional median choice, explains why traversal order removes sorting, and names the single-home and even-home-count boundaries.

The hash-bound Premium Reference remains verified against authenticated source evidence, preserving both examples and their explanation presence, all five constraints, the Manhattan definition, and the informational equivalent of the sole source image.

coverage: Both authenticated source examples appear first, in source order, with their exact grids and minimum distances.
The invented one-home sample was removed because it violates the source guarantee of at least two friends; the formerly hidden asymmetric case is now a visible trial.
Minimum friend count, one-row and one-column grids, maximum width 200, and maximum height 200 cover the material contract boundaries without introducing illegal inputs.

Sparse corners, diagonal endpoints, dense even and odd grids, repeated coordinates with an outlier, an empty optimal cell, and asymmetric coordinates exercise odd and even medians, multiple optima, and independent row and column selection.

An independent exhaustive meeting-cell oracle verified all 13 authored results, all three benchmark results, and the protected source on 9,319 legal grids across shapes up to 4 by 4 with at most 12 cells.
All 13 correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 64-, 256-, and 1,024-cell scaling workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
